content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "F-47 (program element 0207110F) is a U.S. Air Force research-and-development program funded in the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "672088fd457c742c"}}, {"text": "The F-47 is designed to enable air superiority for the Joint Force in the most challenging operational environments, with key attributes including enhancements to survivability, lethality, persistence, crewed/uncrewed teaming, and interoperability.", "citation": {"fact_id": "0247bc1e73bfc103"}}, {"text": "Program activities include digital engineering, agile software development, open systems architectures, and the design, build, and test of full weapon systems, funding operational concept exploration, technology studies, prototyping, and Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) of the F-47 and related technologies.", "citation": {"fact_id": "0247bc1e73bfc103"}}, {"text": "The F-47 program grew out of Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD) Platform work, informed by the Air Force Chief of Staff-approved Air Superiority Enterprise Capability Collaboration Team Flight Plan, which matured technology and reduced risk through development, integration, and test activities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "4c57c16abb689332"}}, {"text": "A related Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) effort develops uncrewed weapon systems capable of enhancing crewed aircraft's ability to achieve air superiority, emphasizing platform cost, mission-integrated autonomy, multi-platform interoperability, and lethality.", "citation": {"fact_id": "4b3360a1bb2d3b73"}}, {"text": "The 2030+ Air Dominance effort conducts operational analyses, threat studies, technology assessments, and prototyping — including the analyses that informed the F-47 Analysis of Alternatives — to identify concepts and technologies that improve persistence, survivability, lethality, connectivity, interoperability, and affordability in 2030 and beyond.", "citation": {"fact_id": "7ab062700549cbda"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding rises from $2,424,208 thousand (about $2.4 billion) in FY2025 to $3,479,362 thousand (about $3.5 billion) requested for FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "630ce8302bdd3f19"}}, {"text": "That is a year-over-year increase of $1,055,154 thousand (about $1.1 billion) from FY2025 to FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "c42bd1434b1b7b41"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the program recorded actual spending of $2,346,905 thousand (about $2.3 billion), so the FY2026 request is roughly half again as large as that recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b15d66f5357802ed"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request splits into a discretionary request of $2,579,362 thousand (about $2.6 billion) and a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $900,000 thousand (about $900 million).", "citation": {"fact_id": "282af51cee5c509f"}}, {"text": "The $900,000 thousand reconciliation request is additional mandatory funding on top of the discretionary base, together making up the program's $3,479,362 thousand FY2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b9bf7d66404c8199"}}, {"text": "The discretionary portion of the request flows through the single named F-47 project, funded at $2,579.362 million for the budget year.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e405df1f4649e9c5"}}, {"text": "The program's own budget narrative states that the mandatory funds address Air Superiority in FY2026, with further detail provided in Section 20007 (Air Superiority) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "768b07f948bf4c45"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "282af51cee5c509f"}}, {"text": "In FY2025 the program was carried under the Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD) Platform project, funded at $2,424.208 million that year before transitioning to the named F-47 project line in FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ce34f48cbc1245fe"}}, {"text": "The F-47 acquisition strategy uses digital acquisition — digital engineering, agile software development, and open systems architectures — with technologies made available to other Department of Defense systems based on emerging threats, Air Force priorities, and development capacity.", "citation": {"fact_id": "0247bc1e73bfc103"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
